newsitem.title: FRANCE: All to gain if Europe no longer means austerity.
newsitem.headline: All to gain if Europe no longer means austerity.

text.p: French Socialist party spokesman Francois Hollande said on Monday the centre-right and left agreed on the need to have the best possible negotiating position on a single currency and all stood to gain if Europe no longer meant austerity.

"We all stand to gain if Italy and Spain are in monetary union, if there is a political government alongside the European Central Bank, if Europe no longer means austerity," he said in a radio interview.

"I believe that President (Jacques Chirac) is committed, like all French people, to have the best possible negotiation for France and for Europe at the time of the switch to the single currency," he said.
He was speaking following a parliamentary election which swept the left to power, ousting the ruling centre-right coalition.

"You can have the single currency without policies restricting public spending, without privatisations, without raising taxes," he added, saying the Socialist party programme did not conflict with plans for monetary union.
The Socialists would, however, make budget savings if necessary, after an audit of public finances due to be carried out in the next two weeks.
